paragraphs: Rav Shmuel bar Marta. ‘The brother of R' Hiyya’—that is, Marta was R' Hiyya's sibling. It is not known whether Marta was a man or a woman. Yuhasin writes in a gloss: Sh.S. said, “If it were a woman's name, it would not have been mentioned in Sanhedrin before R' Hiyya, where it says ‘Ayvu, Hana, Shila, Marta, and Hiyya.’ But if it lists them in birth order, that is satisfactory.” End of quotation. See above, Marta: his stating a halakhah in R' Yehoshua's name proves that he was a man, not a woman. R' Illa: see his entry. Rav Yitzhak reports in R' Shmuel bar Marta's name, who said in Rav's name: Jerusalem Hallah, first chapter, halakhah 5. R' Yitzhak was his son. Rabbah bar bar Hana said: R' Shmuel bar Marta said in Rav's name, in the name of R' Yose of Hutzal: Arvei Pesahim, 113, end of side b. “Rabbah bar bar Hana said: (Rav) Shmuel bar Marta said”—this is the correct reading: Bava Kamma 51b.
